# E18 T1 report

Status: built up to the owner's inputs. No HealthBench score, clinical result, holdout run or gate verdict exists,
and none can until Q-E18-1 (grader credential) and Q-E18-2 (evaluation owner and labels) are answered. The PR body
(#36) carries the gate results and the open items.

## HealthBench (E18-02)

- `healthbench fetch` verifies (or streams) the three pinned files into the ignored `eval/vault/healthbench/`; on
  2026-11-15 all three matched the recorded SHA-256 values.
- `preregister`, `plan`, `generate`, `grade` and `report` run end to end: `tests/test_healthbench_cli.py` on a
  synthetic dataset, `tests/run_real_sample.py` on the real files, both with loopback stand-ins for llama-server and
  the grader. Real-sample run with a 5 s self-test budget: N after warm-up exclusion and preregistered n were main
  4997 and 20, Hard 997 and 17, Consensus 3668 and 18 (n follows the measured warm-up time, so it moves with machine load: a rerun under
  load gave 6, 2 and 3). The main run generated 19, stopped on the budget (one `not_run`, labeled `partial`), made
  235 grader calls and published five schema-valid artifacts with no prompt, rubric, canary or key text. Its numbers
  are not results.
- Without `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `grade` refuses with `grader_credential_missing` (exit 6) and records nothing.
- System-assisted track: `generate` refuses with `no_evaluation_entry_point` (exit 6, nothing recorded) until E13's
  `BenchmarkAnswerPort` exists; with a structural stand-in port the track runs end to end through `report`.
- `eval/bench/fingerprints/healthbench.fp.json`: salted, sampled 8-gram fingerprints of all 5000 examples; the leak
  scan of `model/` and `config/` against it finds nothing.

## Product suites (E18-03) and holdout (E18-01)

- `suite plan | generate | grade | report`, `gate` and `compare` are wired. Without E21's harness they refuse with
  `harness_unavailable` or `provider_missing` (exit 6) before anything is planned or recorded.
- `tests/test_suite_cli.py` proves every command on loopback stand-in hubs built from the contract examples: freeze,
  vault seal, plan, generate (refused while `CHC_EVAL_IDENTITY` or the grader key is set, refused on a LIVE hub),
  grade from the vault in a later process, report, gate and compare. The rules-only track stops the model through
  `setAssistantRuntime` and the recorder counts no model request.
- `NoUnauthorizedExecution` cannot be graded on driver runs: no declared interface exposes denied tool calls or their
  side effects. The gate therefore refuses every driver run with a detail naming that check. The verdict path is
  tested on real published runs with that one outcome set synthetically, and labeled so.
- Holdout cases and labels are the owner's to author; none are invented. The D2 label rule is the `suites.json`
  `label_constraints` row.

## Mutation survivors

`eval/bench/mutation-results.txt`: 748 mutants, 741 killed, 7 survived, 0 without tests. Each survivor is
equivalent:

- `gate` mutants 1 and 2 (`or` to `and` in the empty-input guard): the input they let through is refused later in
  `gate` or `_validate` with the same `gate_input_invalid`.
- `_root` mutants 4, 5 and 6 (the reason of its last raise): unreachable, because `_union` always points the larger
  root at the smaller one, so the parent walk cannot cycle.
- `_near_pairs` mutants 22 (`key = None`) and 25 (`(band - 1) * width`): they only put more cases in one LSH bucket.
  Exact Jaccard confirms every candidate pair, so the groups do not change.

## Corrections to the design

- 5.2: simple-evals has no packaging at the pinned commit, so it is vendored as a wheel of unedited upstream bytes.
- 5.4: full HealthBench fingerprints exceed 40 MB; a modulus sample keeps containment unbiased at 4.4 MB.
- 12: E18 test markers `e18`, `v33` and `v34` exist only in the bench project; the hub's strict markers allow only
  `trace`, `slow`, `hardware` and `E01`, so the hub scenario carries `trace` only.
- The process clock moved from the hub kernel into `crew_health_bench.adapters.clock`: the kernel import contract
  forbids wall clock reads in kernel code.
